description: Append one durable fact about the owner to their memory file: a preference, a correction on how to work, a project constraint, or a reference. It becomes part of brain_identity immediately. Include why it matters and how to apply it. When it changes an earlier fact, pass `replaces` with that fact's id (the stamp in its heading, e.g. '2026-09-22 18:21'): the old fact stays in the file as history and leaves brain_identity. For a fact with one current value, pass `subject` and `attribute` (e.g. 'JobMail' and 'database'); a later fact with the same pair replaces it on its own. Use `valid_until` for something temporary and `valid_from` when it became true earlier than now. Near-duplicates of current facts are refused, and a fact that looks like it changes a current one is held back until you say whether it replaces it; pass force=true to store it as is. Do not store session trivia.

attribute.description: Which property of the subject, e.g. 'database' or 'employer'. Pass with subject.

category.description: user = who they are; feedback = how to work with them; project = ongoing work; reference = pointer

force.description: Store even if it looks like a duplicate or a change to a current fact

replaces.description: Ids of current facts this one makes outdated, e.g. ['2026-09-22 18:21']

subject.description: What the fact is about, e.g. 'JobMail' or 'the owner'. Pass with attribute.

valid_from.description: When it became true, if earlier or later than now: YYYY-MM-DD or YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (UTC)

valid_until.description: When it stops being true, for temporary facts: YYYY-MM-DD (holds through that day) or YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (UTC)

name: brain_remember
title: Remember a durable fact
